title: DocstringStepNumberingMismatch
description: The `@notice` step-numbering header above run() drifts from the run() body and the in-body section headers. registerDispatcher is documented as step 9 in the @notice block but is step 8 in the body; setDispatcherIndex is documented as step 3 in the @notice block but is step 9 in the body. The actual execution ordering in the body is correct; only the docstring numbering is wrong.
impact: Documentation-only. No behavioral defect: the run() ordering is correct and the on-chain effect is unaffected. The mismatch can mislead an operator reading the header during a resume/triage. No security or availability impact.
evidence: @notice header numbers registerDispatcher as step 9; run() body executes it as step 8.
@notice header numbers setDispatcherIndex as step 3; run() body executes it as step 9.
Section headers inside run() agree with the body, not with the @notice block.
Execution order is correct; the discrepancy is confined to the docstring.
recommendation: Renumber the @notice step block to match the run() body and its section headers so the documented sequence equals the executed sequence.
